name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year; next release 4 Dec
state: The FAO Food Price Index averaged 133.9 points in October, published on 6 Nov, down 1.2% from September and 5.9% above a year earlier (FAO). Cereals fell 4.5% and meat and dairy eased, while sugar rose 6.6% for a fourth monthly gain to its highest since December 2024. The annual rise meets the Watch line; the index is below the 135 Alert line and no new staple export bans by several major exporters were found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Households and food importers face food costs higher than a year ago, with sugar and vegetable oils rising fastest. Price moves on world markets usually reach shop prices with a lag of several months.
rubric_hit: FFPI y/y +5.9% > +5% Watch line; 133.9 < 135 Alert line

sources.title: FAO — FAO Food Price Index edges down in October amid subdued demand

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
